newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 24.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:

* Stocks dropped in a late-day sell-off in the busiest trading day in the history of the New York Stock Exchange. The Dow Jones industrials fell 94.28 points to close at 6,755.75 and Nasdaq closed at 1,378.37.
* PepsiCo said it will spin off its restaurant business and possibly sell its food service unit.
* Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co said it will acquire Amphenol Corp for $1.05 billion plus debt.
* General Motors is expected to increase its dividend and begin a large stock buyback program on Monday.
* Treasury Secretery Robert Rubin is considering a proposal to let banks own and be owned by commercial companies.
* The U.S. government had a budget surplus in December, but its deficit for the first three months of 1997 was 5.4 percent bigger than that for the year-ago period.
* The Federal Reserve Board says America's wealth was spread more evenly in the first half of the decade.
* Sega Enterprises agrees to buy Bandai Co Ltd in a stock deal valued at $1.09 billion.
* CompuServ will tweak America Online and its service problems in ads to run before the Super Bowl.
* Sears fourth quarter profits rose 25 percent, but the company also had higher chargeoffs on credit card receivables.
* McDonald's posted a 12 percent rise in fourth quarter earnings despite a 48.7 million charge.
* Boeing and McDonnell Douglas earnings met analysts' expecations.
* Bankers Trust fourth quarter net came in below expectations.
* Chevron, Texaco, Occidental Petroleum and other oil companies reported better than expected quarterly profits.
* Xerox reported fourth quarter net above expectations. It also agreed to sell two units and raise its dividend.

* The Vinik effect is back. This time it's being felt in the market for small and microcap stocks, where Jeffrey Vinik, the former high-profile manager of Fidelity Investments' Magellan fund, lately has been scooping up big holdings through his new hedge fund. -- Heard on the Street.

* Treasury securities gave more ground in cautious trading, as investors focused on a growing supply of bonds and showed no interest in making large bets ahead of next week's release of economic data. -- Credit Markets.
